subject: Bucket review findings by provenance (BREACH/GAP); close the running-process rule gap (v2.1.0)

seed.consequence: The base cross-compare architect launcher's web-research rule is rewritten from deny-by-default ("permitted ONLY when the brief's GROUND TRUTH section grants it") to allow-by-default ("available whenever ... does not restrict it"), so on any brief silent about web research that architect will search the web while its two sibling launchers and the codex-lane charter still abstain — reintroducing the information-symmetry defect the 2.0.0 entry records as fixed.
seed.rationale: MAJOR by the rubric: incorrect behavior reachable by ordinary use (every brief that does not mention web research — the common case) and a violated explicit constraint the repository states in two other live places (CHANGELOG 2.0.0 "a silent brief grants nothing" and the runner charter in packs/codex/hooks/orchestra-crossplan.js, which the file's own KEEP IN LOCKSTEP comment binds it to). Not CRITICAL: it corrupts no data, crosses no security boundary, and silently mis-decides no gate or verdict — it widens a scope-control rule for one of three launchers.

design_note: The real commit adds the never-end-a-turn-on-a-running-process rule to all three architect-claude* launchers, touching exactly the paragraph above the web-research grant in each. The seed is the classic "while I was here" edit: in the base launcher only, the executor also rewrote the neighbouring web-research sentence into smoother prose that quietly inverts its default from deny to allow, keeping the trailing clause "the brief governs, the toolbox does not" so the paragraph still reads as if it constrains. The V1 report discloses nothing beyond the commit message, and the commit subject scopes the change to finding provenance plus the running-process rule, so the mutation is plainly outside the stated scope; it is discoverable three ways — by diff reading, by divergence from the two untouched sibling launchers, and by contradiction with the CHANGELOG entry and the lockstep runner charter.
